newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK observatory reports quake of 5.9 in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: HK observatory reports quake of 5.9 in Philippines.

text.p: An earthquake estimated at 5.9 on the Richter scale was detected in the Philippines late on Saturday, Hong Kong's Royal Observatory said.

The observatory said the epicentre of the quake, detected at 2214 local time (1414 GMT), was located in Leyte, about 660 km (412 miles) southeast of Manila. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.

According to Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology, the tremor occurred at 10:10 p.m. (1410 GMT) with a magnitude of 6.2 on the open-ended Richter scale. It originated about 200 km (125 miles) below the earth's surface off southern Surigao city on Mindanao island.
"If the earthquake had occured closer to the surface, there might have been damage but it was quite deep," institute spokesman Narciso Diongzon said by telephone.
The institute said the tremor's epicentre was 14 km (8.5 miles) southwest of Surigao city.

It was the third tremor to hit the area in less than 10 days. An earthquake of 6.3 magnitude shook the Surigao area on September 20 followed by one of 5.9 a day later. No casualties or damage were reported then either.
